name: Mitochondrial DNA Depletion Syndrome, Hepatocerebral Form

ethnicAssociations: Reported worldwide without specific ethnic predilection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes

criteria.description: Progressive liver failure with hepatomegaly and elevated liver enzymes
Neurological manifestations including developmental delay, hypotonia, and seizures
Demonstration of mitochondrial DNA depletion in liver or muscle biopsy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in nuclear genes involved in mtDNA maintenance (e.g., POLG, DGUOK, MPV17)
Elevated serum lactate and metabolic acidosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive hepatic dysfunction and neurological involvement combined with confirmed mitochondrial DNA depletion on tissue biopsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and guide prognosis.

searchTerms: enlarged liver with worsening liver failure
marked low muscle tone in infancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked mitochondrial DNA depletion in liver tissue
searchTerms: marked mitochondrial DNA loss in liver
severe mitochondrial DNA shortage in liver tissue
very low mitochondrial DNA in liver

occasional.symptomName: Failure of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes

imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral atrophy and basal ganglia abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in POLG, DGUOK, MPV17, or other nuclear genes involved in mtDNA maintenance
Confirmed mitochondrial DNA depletion in liver or muscle biopsy
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers and decreased respiratory chain enzyme activities

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent progressive neurological deterioration without early liver failure
POLG mutations but distinct clinical course
Lack of mitochondrial DNA depletion on biopsy
Absence of neurological involvement early in disease
Predominant myopathic or encephalomyopathic presentations without significant liver involvement

redFlags: Rapidly progressive liver failure in infancy
Elevated serum lactate with metabolic acidosis
references: El-Hattab AW, Scaglia F. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes: review and updates of genetic basis, manifestations, and therapeutic options. Neurotherapeutics. 2013;10(2):186-198.
Spinazzola A, Zeviani M. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes: clinical features and molecular mechanisms. Neurogenetics. 2009;10(3):151-158.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome, hepatocerebral form. ORPHA:254871.
